thread:
alex: seeing a sudden cluster of blocked GPU attaches in ap-south1, related to local NVMe flaps. noticed attach failures and delayed provisioning since 09:12 UTC :confused:
ops-bot: ALERT: node=gnode-apse1-433 nvme_i/o_errors=127 scrub_queue_depth=74
maya: confirmed, logs show a huge KV-cache spill from a big model load -> tinywrites train causing write amplification
lee: that rings a bell — we saw similar smallwrite bursts last month but not this magnitude
maya: snippet from node logs:
```
2026-03-23T09:12:03Z kvcache: spill-start size=18.4GB keys=1.2M
2026-03-23T09:12:03Z nvme: submit_bio: len=4KB qdepth=128 ret=EIO
2026-03-23T09:12:05Z scrub: enqueue 1200 async metadata writes
```
sam: any immediate mitigation? we have queued GPU jobs waiting, costs piling up with retries
maya: short term: throttle kvcache spill concurrency and slow janitor cadence to reduce overlapping fsyncs
alex: can we patch the cleaner on ap-south1 to reduce parallel scrubs to 1 for now?
lee: +1. config we can flip via rollout: `janitor.max_parallel_scrubs = 1` and `kvcache.spill_batch_size = 64MB`
nirav: I'll push a canary to 5% of ap-south1 first. estimating attach success rate improvement from 62% -> ~90% if I/O contention drops
sam: timeline? we should also notify capacity-planning, jobs are backlogged ~120 GPU-hours
maya: ops-bot: create incident stub and link to node group, tag @capacity-team :point_up:
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0323-01 - nvme smallwrite spike ap-south1 (link)
lee: also digging into firmware counters, suspect controller power management toggles coinciding with spill start. scheduling read of SMART and thermal logs
alex: anything we can do to avoid repeat? longer term ideas?
maya: two things: 1) avoid single-request KV spills by limiting model-load concurrency per node, 2) pre-warm prefix cache to reduce large spill events during peak deployment windows
nirav: cost note: if we keep throttling scrubs we slow reclamation -> latent wear increases S3 egress for replica repairs. need a tradeoff approval from infra leads
sam: raising with infra leads now. temporary fix first, then postmortem and cost calc
lee: rolling the canary patch now: `kubectl apply -f /ops/configs/janitor-throttle-apse1.yaml`
ops-bot: deploy started by nirav at 2026-03-23T09:14:12Z
nirav: canary applied to 8 nodes, monitoring iostat + attach success
alex: nice. please update INC with results and ETA for fleet-wide roll
maya: early telemetry: node iops down 35%, attach success up to 84% on canary nodes :thumbsup:
sam: good enough to expand to 50%?
lee: wait 10m for stability, also queueing smart counters to check for increased re-writes
sre-bot: scheduled job: collect-smart --nodes=canary --every=30s --out=/tmp/smart-apse1-canary.log
alex: thanks all — we'll reconvene in 20 to decide fleet roll. assigning followups: sam -> coord infra leads, nirav -> expand canary, lee -> firmware/SMART dive, maya -> write postmortem draft
maya: adding a quick checklist to the incident: causes, mitigation, perf metrics, cost impact, permanent mitigations
ops-bot: INC-2026-0323-01 updated with checklist
alex: :white_check_mark: closing loop later. if anything regresses ping here immediately
